findings.label: Microcytic hypochromic red cells on blood smear
findings.evidence: marked microcytosis (arrowheads); in-text mentions target cells

panels.rationale: Peripheral blood smear from a patient in an alpha-thalassemia case report shows marked microcytosis, supporting a microcytic thalassemic manifestation. The coexisting sickled erythrocytes reflect sickle cell trait, so attribution to hemoglobin H disease is not definitive and confidence is moderate.
panels.attribution_text: Chuquimarca et al. Alpha-Thalassemia Unmasked in a Patient With Sickle Cell Trait: A Case Report.. Cureus 2025. doi:10.7759/cureus.92353. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 1.
panels.figure_caption: Peripheral blood smear (May-Grünwald Giemsa stain, 100× oil immersion). The image shows red blood cells with marked microcytosis (arrowheads) and occasional sickled erythrocytes (open circle). No nucleated red blood cells were observed.
in_text_mentions: The peripheral blood smear demonstrated microcytosis, target cells, and occasional sickled erythrocytes (Figure 1). Capillary electrophoresis revealed HbA at 70%, HbS at 26.8%, and HbA2 at 3.2% (Table 2), consistent with sickle cell trait. However, the patient’s HbS level was lower than expected for sickle trait, and in the context of significant microcytosis without iron deficiency, this finding raised suspicion of coexisting alpha-thalassemia.
